summary: Mireille Bénisti (1909–1993) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She earned diplomas from the École du Louvre and École Pratique des Hautes Études, held posts at the CNRS and Musées Nationaux, and taught at the École du Louvre.

Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She served as Chargé de Recherche at the CNRS from circa 1967 to 1993 and had an attested affiliation with Paris Nanterre University in 1985.

Mirella Keller specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed an MA at Fo Guang University (2015–2018) and a PhD at Eötvös Loránd University (2019), where she was a PhD student (2019–2025) before becoming assistant professor at Dharma Gate Buddhist College in 2025.

Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. Her affiliations attested in 2026 include serving as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich and holding a post at the University of Tübingen.

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA from the University of Otago and a PhD from the University of Calgary (2005) under John A. Baker, later holding posts at the University of New South Wales and University of Western Australia.

Miriam Levering (1943–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She received her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.

Mirjan Damaška (born 1931) studied at the University of Zagreb and completed a PhD at the University of Ljubljana in 1960. He held academic posts at Zagreb, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale University, where he became Sterling Professor emeritus.

Miron Winslow (1789–1864) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Middlebury College (circa 1813–1815) and Andover Theological Seminary (circa 1815–1818), and founded the American Madras Mission in 1836.

Miroslav Marcovich (1919–2001) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at the University of Belgrade. He taught at Belgrade, the University of Los Andes, and served as Professor of Classics at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1969–1989), with appointments at Bonn and Cambridge.
Mitashree Srivastava works in Buddhist studies. She earned an M.Sc from the University of Allahabad in 2007 and was appointed Associate Professor at the University of Delhi in 2013.
Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher and served as a professor at the University of Basel.

Mithilesh Chaturvedi works in Indology and linguistics. He was affiliated with the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (attested 2009) and later served as Professor emeritus there (attested 2026).

Mitsuji Fukunaga (1918–2001) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University. He held professorships at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University (1982–1986), and the University of Kitakyushu (1986–1989).
Mitsukuni Yoshida (1921–1991) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University circa 1942–1945 and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts circa 1986–1991.
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer between 1989 and 1995.
Mitsuyo Demoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and was affiliated with the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa (1923–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned doctorates at the University of Munich and Kokugakuin University, later holding professorships at Tsukuba and Nihon University.

Mitsuyuki Ishida (1911–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a teacher and professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1948 to 1976 and as a professor at Shitennoji University in 1976.

Mittal Trivedi is an Indologist and linguist who earned an Acharya degree from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (2017–2019) and was a doctoral student (dottorandi) at the University of Cagliari from 2020 to 2024.
Miyako Notake specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, holding posts as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Waseda University attested in 2015 and 2026.
